t:
(a) 
Report on Levels of the Ogallala Aquifer.—Title III of the Water Resources Research Act of 1984 (42 U.S.C. 10301 note) is amended—

        (1) 
in section 306, by striking “annually” and inserting “biennially”; and
 
        (2) 
in section 308, by striking “intervals of one year” and inserting “intervals of 2 years”.
  
    (b) 
Report on Effects of Outer Continental Shelf Leasing Activities on Human, Marine, and Coastal Environments.—Section 20(e) of the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act (43 U.S.C. 1346(e)) is amended by striking “each fiscal year” and inserting “every 3 fiscal years”.

fable.w: This section only changes how often two existing reports are due (annual to biennial, and yearly to every three fiscal years). The tempting reading is that reporting provisions imply some consultation, but nothing here brings states, experts, the public or any other outside party into a federal decision. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue.
fable.s: Report on Levels of the Ogallala Aquifer.

qwen_block.w: This section merely amends the frequency of reports required by other statutes. It does not establish any mechanism for outside parties to consult with, advise, or participate in federal decision-making. The text describes internal reporting schedules rather than public participation processes.
qwen_block.s: Report on Levels of the Ogallala Aquifer.—Title III of the Water Resources Research Act of 1984 (42 U.S.C. 10301 note) is amended— (1) in section 306, by striking “annually” and inserting “biennially”; and (2) in section 308, by striking “intervals of one year” and inserting “intervals of 2 years”.

opus.w: The section only changes how often existing federal reports are due. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is consulted, and no rulemaking, hearing or right to sue is created. Reporting requirements look procedural, but they stay inside the federal government and do not bring outsiders into a decision.
opus.s: is amended by striking “each fiscal year” and inserting “every 3 fiscal years”.
opus.b:
This section only changes how often two reports are due. The Ogallala Aquifer report moves from annual to every 2 years. The report on the effects of Outer Continental Shelf leasing moves from every fiscal year to every 3 fiscal years.

The tempting reading is that reporting sounds procedural. That fails because no one outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision. The section has no comment period, hearing, consultation, advisory body or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely amends the frequency of statutory reports from annual to biennial or triennial. It does not establish any mechanism for public participation, consultation with outside entities, or advisory committees. The reports are internal government documents submitted to Congress or other federal bodies, which falls under the 'No' category for intra-governmental communication.
qwen_chat.s: in section 306, by striking “annually” and inserting “biennially”; and ... in section 308, by striking “intervals of one year” and inserting “intervals of 2 years”. ... Section 20(e) of the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act (43 U.S.C. 1346(e)) is amended by striking “each fiscal year” and inserting “every 3 fiscal years”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the reports are about environmental effects or aquifer levels, they might involve public input. However, the text only specifies the frequency of the reports (biennially or every 3 years) and does not mention any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory boards. The reports are submitted by federal agencies (implied by the statutes being amended) to Congress or other federal bodies, which is internal government communication.
